recipes.name: Six Can Chicken Tortilla Soup
ingredients_raw: 1 (15 ounce) can whole kernel corn, drained
1 (10 ounce) can diced tomatoes with green chile peppers, drained

steps.text: Pour chicken broth, corn, black beans, chunk chicken, and diced tomatoes with green chiles into a large saucepan or stockpot over medium heat.
Simmer, stirring occasionally, until chicken is heated through, about 15 minutes.
Serve hot, topped with tortilla chips and shredded cheese.

raw_recipe.headline: Six Can Chicken Tortilla Soup
raw_recipe.description: This easy chicken tortilla soup recipe uses cans of corn, chicken broth, black beans, chunk chicken, and tomatoes for a tasty meal on busy weeknights.

video.description: See how to make simple tortilla soup using basic ingredients commonly found in the pantry.

review.reviewBody: Doctor it up! I've made this recipe for over a year and passed it along by request. It's a definite 5 star, especially for your time invested. However, you MUST add seasoning. This recipe gives you the base. I would rate it 2-3 stars without additions. My suggestions...substitute 1/2 broth with Cream of Chicken soup. Rinse your black beans well! Add cumin and chili powder...don't be shy. It gives your soup depth. Add cilantro and garlic powder, if available. Grab a rotiserie chicken from your grocery. I wouldn't expect a 5 star recipe to have canned chicken, would you? Serve with chunked avocados, cheese, a squeeze of lime and whatever else your heart desires. Good luck!

This recipe is so quick, easy, and cheap...just open the cans and boil. I only spent about $10.00 on ingredients. My company thought it was really good. After reading the other reviews, here's what I came up with which was perfect: I only used one can of chicken broth (not condensed or it will be too salty), I added 2 cans of condensed cream of chicken soup so it wasn't too watery as other reviewers suggested, used a milder version of tomatoes with green chiles (Rotel tomatoes with lime/cilantro work well). Be sure to rinse the beans and make sure to season with garlic powder, salt, peper, chili powder, and cumin otherwise there won't be much flavor. Many reviewers suggested adding cilantro which I will try next time. Top with sour cream, cheddar cheese and some tortilla chips and it is perfect. You really can't go wrong with this one.

Ok, I don't exactly follow this recipe but it gave me some great ideas. I've cooked variations several times now - the ingredients depend on what I have on hand.

Here's a sample of what I've put in at different times - Carrots, dark and white chicken breasts I've browned in butter, allowed to cool, and shredded, canned diced green chile, green chile enchilada sauce, rice, green onions, yellow onion, canned corn, can of kidney beans, minced fresh garlic or garlic powder, red chile powder, the list goes on and on. 

It's quick to prepare - but tastes best when I put it in the slow cooker and let the flavors really infuse for about 6 hours but one time I made it quickly with rice, chicken, green chiles, and canned corn - and sent it with my husband when he was visiting his sick mom. GET THIS! She can't stop raving about it!! She brags about my cooking to everyone now!! This is a miracle recipe! 

Don't worry if you don't have all the ingredients or want to add other stuff - just use what you have and people will love it!!

I have made this recipe so many times and always with rave reviews, which is saying a lot from my picky husband! As well as others, I use one can of cream of chicken soup in place of the 2 cans of chicken broth and I don't drain the can of diced tomatoes and chiles so it is still "soupy", I also use a can of mexican corn, drained or frozen corn if I have it on hand instead. I drain and rinse the black beans because I prefer them that way. While the soup is simmering I heat the oven to 350 and use a pizza wheel to cut flour tortillas in small, thin strips, bake them for a few minutes until crispy and top the soup with those and a dollop of sour cream. This recipe will remain in my kitchen for years to come and there are so many things you can do to change it up. Thanks for a great recipe!!

I make something very similar, but it needs some more ingredients. Saute a diced onion in 1 TBSP oil until translucent. Add 2-3 cloves minced garlic and saute for 30 sec. Add 1 TBSP cumin and 2 TBSP chili powder. 2 cans corn (drained), 1 can black beans (drained and rinsed) 2 can tomatoes with green chilis. Chicken broth to desired consistancy (less for a stew-like consistancy, more for soup). I add a TBSP better than bullion chicken. Cook for 20-30 min. Serve over crushed tortilla chips. Top with crumbled Queso Fresco, diced avocado, sour cream, and lime juice. Use a skinned rotisserie chicken as an option.

Sautéed a small white onion and 1 jalapeño in 1 tablespoon of canola oil. 1/4 tsp of cayenne pepper. Low sodium chicken broth. I used shredded chicken from the deli. Frozen corn. The rest of ingredients as written. Topped with tortilla strips, fresh cilantro and shredded cheese. Served with crusty baguette. Everyone loved this soup. Thanks for sharing. I make a big pot of soup every Saturday during fall-winter. It’s a long season here in Minnesota.

The way it is would be perfect emergency or last minute dinner. I’ve made it for years-better if you can sauté chicken breast in good seasoning first, take it out and let it rest, then add the rotel/tomatoes and chiles and the broth to the same pot and use an immersion blender (my husband hates seeing tomatoes), then add the corn and drained and rinsed beans, chop the chicken and put it back, then add Tajin and white or black or red pepper and let it simmer a little while super low-then serve with lime and avocado and cheese and tortilla chips it’s so good

Was excellent, and a time saver. Started this at lunch, and dinner was ready after work. Used 1 can broth, 1 can cream of chicken, rinsed black beans, mild rotel, Mexican can corn, 1 bag frozen diced chicken, 1 Tbsp taco seasoning, about 1/4 of chopped onion. Stirred in crockpot for high 5 hrs. Prep took less than 10 mins, very simple, and will add to rotation! 👍

This is a straightforward recipe, but it is bland. It needs a little dressing up. I added 1/2 teaspoon of Salt, 1/4 teaspoon of black pepper, 1 teaspoon of cumin, 1 teaspoon of chili powder, another can of black beans, and a total of 32 ounces of chicken stock. In my book that elivated the soup to four stars.

I used some rotisserie chicken breast instead of canned. I started by sautéing chopped onion and celery, adding minced garlic near the end of that, then added the cream of chicken soup, rinsed black beans and corn. I used a can of regular diced tomatoes and threw in some salsa verde I found. I seasoned with cumin, chili powder, garlic and onion powders and Frank's Hot Sauce (since I didn't have any taco seasoning). I added a couple cups of water to thin it out some. I also had some stale-ish tortillas that I sliced up and put on a 13x9 cookie sheet lightly sprayed with Pam in a 350 degree oven, 3 mins on each side and was surprised at how tasty those crispy strips were! It totally took the soup to the next level! I'll be making this meal again!

I gave it 2 stars because nobody liked it as is. The next time, I made several changes taken from the reviews and added one of my own, so it's no longer the same recipe. But, my family loves the changes. So what I did was buy rotisserie chicken, strip it down and put meat aside. Boiled the carcass in 4 c water for an hour or so, letting water cook down some. Strained the water into Dutch oven, added 2 cans cream of chicken and a can of green chopped chilis and a can of creamed corn in addition to recipe. Garlic powder, onion powder, chili powder, cumin, 2 pinches cinnamon and 2 pinches of sugar. Lastly added the chicken, shredded up and heated it all to comfortable eating temp. Served with cheddar & cotillo cheeses, tortilla strips and sliced Mexican green onions and some avocado cubes. My son added hot sauce to his bowl. Creamy without being too thick or too soupy. Boiling step can be replaced with canned broth, of course and recipe is still easy peasy; just a bit "eh" (for us) as written.

Okay... added a heaping tsp of Siete chicken fajita mix. Also added 1 can of pinto beans 1/4 cup chopped red onion. Finally 2 tbsp of idahoan buttery homestyle mashed potatoes. Topped with avocado & sour cream We ate with chili lime tortilla chips. This was gluten free & amazing! Thanks AR
Great simple meal on a budget, for those nights when you don’t have the time, I added a can of cream of chicken to replace some of the broth, you can add whatever you and your family like
So simple yet satisfying! I use cayenne pepper, onion and garlic powder and chili powder to add a kick!! Yummy
Easy and quick recipe. Tasty!
So good, I always tweak things and dont measure but garlic juice and fire roasted rotel is a must and lime juice on top with baked tortilla strips drizzled iv evoo ❤️ and parm chunks and shreds

The amount of people talking about how they needed to add something to this to make it better, or how the fresh chicken is better is insane. It's literally a meal you can make with very little effort. If I didn't have a lot of time to worry about dinner, but wanted something that tasted good, this would be an excellent last minute back up. It took me a total of 3 minutes to dump the cans into a pot, and then spend the next half hour watching a movie before enjoying it while it heated up. Yes, you CAN add a bunch of stuff to it, cook chicken and whatever to make it taste better, but that's not the point. This is a meal you can have sitting in your closet for half a year and bring it out at any time with so little fuss you barely have to think about it. It's like a lifesaver for families who need to feed themselves, but don't have the time to spend three hours making lasagna. I get talking about what you added to it to make it better; when I cook I always look at the comments to see different possibilities and a lot of the time I go with those recommendations. But to downvote it because it wasn't up to expectations is like saying "I didn't like this 10 cent bag of ramen because it didn't have enough meat and spices in it." It's a six can chicken tortilla soup. It ain't winning any Oscars, but it's been added to my closet as something I can throw together with almost no effort and still be filling and taste decent.
I made this. The only thing I did different was. I did not use canned chicken. I used rotisserie chicken, and I also added a little bit of fajita seasoning.

I made this per the recipe the first time and it's good, but I did add an extra can if chicken because my partner likes meat. The second time I made it with ground beef. I rinsed the beans and add a little more chicken stock to replace the liquids. I also added a small can of green chili's and can of green enchiladas sauce for more flavor. The third time I made it with chicken again, two cans but dus what I did in the second time. I love this with any protein you add. It's a quick, easy and yummy meal that this household loves and we make it often.
Just added our own spices and everyone loved it! Super easy and super good!
